notes: Concurrency: up to five panes of this build were registered at the production listener at once across these runs (stall, healthy, the two controls, the two break attempts). Each kept its own row, keyed by its own scratch directory, and no run observed another's row.

What was left behind, as the architect asked. Every pane ran in a fresh /tmp scratch directory with --no-skills --no-rules --no-extensions --no-tools, claimed no Envoy role, and sent no message to any session or topic; the only writes any run made to the listener were the DELETE /v1/sessions calls the recover arm and the delete break attempt are about, plus one cleanup DELETE per run. The smoke script SIGKILLs its pane at exit, so the stall arm's record outlived its process; it was deleted (DELETE -> 200), and `GET /v1/sessions` filtered to these scratch directories now returns zero rows. The scratch directories are removed. One condition was not met: the panes' listener rows carried an empty `title`, so none names itself an INFRA-246 proof - a headless `omp` pane with no title model generates no session name, the smoke script passes no title and `omp` has no flag to set one. The directory (/tmp/smoke-registration-stall-*, /tmp/healthy-pane.*, /tmp/break-pane.*) is what identifies these rows.

Not driven on a real surface, and why: the listener's new boot line naming the resolved session record lifetime (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go) needs a running listener, which needs a NATS server with JetStream. This pod has no nats-server binary and no such module in packages/envoy's go.mod or the module cache, `kubectl auth can-i create services` and `get services` both answer no in the namespace this pod holds credentials for, and booting a second listener against the production NATS would put a second consumer on live subjects. The line is one `logger.Info` over the existing `SessionRegistry.TTL()` accessor, compiled by CI's Go lanes (Legion Envoy and Contracts run 40156837298 success); it carries no behaviour this phase could otherwise break.

Hardening note for the architect, not a failure of this change: `ENVOY_PASS_DEADLINE_MS` (and `ENVOY_HEARTBEAT_MS`, which the deadline defaults to through max(heartbeatMs, 30 s)) is floored at 25 ms but has no ceiling, and a value of 2_147_483_648 ms or more overflows the 32-bit timer - `bun` fires such a setTimeout at once (measured: 'fired after 9 ms'), so every queued task would be abandoned immediately and no pass would ever settle. It takes a value past 24.8 days to reach, and the same overflow already exists for the heartbeat's own setInterval before this change, so it is recorded here rather than pinned by a red test; a one-line clamp in `envoySettings` would close it.
Static lanes were read, not re-run: lint, typecheck and the unit and integration suites are cited from the PR body's CI line at the code head 6ebea43a49, where every run GitHub started is success.
